title: Oman accepts Islam
description: The Julanda brothers who rule Oman accept Islam from Amr ibn al-As, the envoy of Muhammad.

title: First Ibadi imam
description: The Ibadis of the interior elect al-Julanda bin Masud as imam, the start of a tradition of elected imams that lasts twelve centuries.

title: Portuguese sack Muscat
description: Afonso de Albuquerque burns the port, and the Portuguese hold the coast for nearly a century and a half.

title: Ottoman capture of Muscat
description: An Ottoman fleet under Piri Reis takes the town for a short time.

title: Yaruba dynasty founded
description: Nasir bin Murshid is elected imam and unites the tribes against the Portuguese.

title: Portuguese expelled from Muscat
description: Imam Sultan bin Saif takes the last Portuguese forts, and Oman becomes a sea power in the Indian Ocean.

title: Al Said dynasty founded
description: Ahmad bin Said, who drove out the Persians, is elected imam and founds the family that still rules.

title: Treaty with the East India Company
description: The ruler of Muscat signs a first treaty with the British, the start of two centuries of close ties.

title: Said bin Sultan takes power
description: Said begins a reign of fifty years in which Oman's trading empire on the East African coast is at its height.

title: Treaty with the United States
description: Said bin Sultan signs a treaty of friendship and trade with the American envoy Edmund Roberts.

title: Muscat and Zanzibar separated
description: After Said's death a British award divides his lands between two sons, cutting Oman off from the wealth of Zanzibar.

title: Azzan bin Qais takes Muscat
description: An imam backed by the tribes of the interior overthrows the sultan and rules for three years.

title: Imamate revived
description: The tribes of the interior elect Salim al-Kharusi imam and rise against the sultan in Muscat.

title: Treaty of Seeb
description: The sultan recognises the self-government of the imamate in the interior, dividing the country for a generation.

title: Said bin Taimur becomes sultan
description: Said begins a reign of 38 years that pays off the state's debts and keeps the country closed.

title: Jebel Akhdar War
description: With British help the sultan defeats the imamate and brings the interior and its oil under his rule.

title: Gwadar sold to Pakistan
description: The sultan gives up the enclave on the Makran coast that Oman had held since 1783.

title: Dhofar War
description: A rebellion in the southern province, later led by Marxists backed by South Yemen, is defeated with British and Iranian help.

title: First oil exports
description: Oil from the fields of the interior is shipped for the first time.

title: Qaboos overthrows his father
description: Qaboos bin Said takes power in a palace coup, renames the country the Sultanate of Oman and begins to build schools, roads and hospitals.

title: Basic Statute
description: Qaboos issues the country's first written constitution by decree.

title: Cyclone Gonu
description: The strongest cyclone on record in the Arabian Sea floods Muscat and the eastern coast.

title: Protests of 2011
description: Protests for jobs and against corruption lead the sultan to dismiss ministers and give the elected council some powers.
